This project aims to strengthen gender-responsive and inclusive democratic institutions in Bangladesh during a critical period of political reform. It focuses on enhancing the capacity of the Bangladesh Election Commission (BEC) to implement gender-mainstreamed electoral processes, develop the BEC Gender Strategy, and align with CEDAW General Recommendation 40. The initiative will provide targeted training and support through the Election Training Institute (ETI) and BRIDGE-certified facilitators, while institutionalizing feminist approaches within electoral education. This project leads by WAVE Foundation and partnership with Action Aid Bangladesh. Simultaneously, the project empowers civil society organizations and women-led platforms to advocate for inclusive governance and women`s political leadership. It will support national strategy development, civic engagement, and locally driven awareness campaigns, along with a small grants program to strengthen grassroots activism. To address systemic barriers, the project also strengthens referral mechanisms to prevent Violence Against Women in Politics (VAWP), improve coordination between BEC and One-Stop Crisis Centres, and promote safe political participation. The 13-month implementation period across 8 districts and 16 Upazilas under Jamalpur, Patuakhali, Khulna, Bogra, Kurigram, Satkhira, Mymensingh, Cox’s Bazar districts. গ্রাহক সেবা নিশ্চিত করতে সেলস, ভিসা এবং অপারেশনস টিমের সাথে সমন্বয় করা। এয়ারলাইনের নীতিমালা, ভাড়ার নিয়মাবলী এবং কোম্পানির কার্যপদ্ধতি মেনে চলা। দৈনিক/সাপ্তাহিক টিকেটিং এবং বিক্রয় সংক্রান্ত প্রতিবেদন job_description: Name of Project:  Strengthening Climate-smart Vegetable and Flower Value Chain in Bangladesh Assignment Duration:  1 Years Background: SDS (Shariatpur Development Society) is a Bangladesh-based non-governmental organization founded in 1991 and formally registered with the Department of Social Welfare (1992), the NGO Affairs Bureau (1993) and the Microcredit Regulatory Authority (2008). SDS received its first foreign funding in 1994 and established a long-standing partnership with PKSF in 1996. Working primarily in climate-vulnerable areas, SDS addresses climate change-induced vulnerabilities, disaster risks and structural poverty through participatory, inclusive and accountable approaches. SDS has experience working with institutional donors including UNDP, UNICEF, WFP, UN Women, FAO, IOM, CARE, Islamic Relief, CJRF, Barnfonden and START Network members and is actively engaged in national, regional and global networks such as CANSA, GNDR, NEAR, INAFI, APWLD and Girls Not Brides. Currently, SDS is implementing multiple donor-funded projects. For more info please visit  www.sdsbd.org   SDS is implementing the project “Strengthening Climate-smart Vegetable and Flower Value Chain in Bangladesh” with support from Heifer International Bangladesh. The project aims to improve the income and climate-resilient livelihoods of approximately 7,200 smallholder women farmers in Rajbari District Position Purpose: The Community Facilitator will implement project activities at the community and field levels. The position will mobilize and strengthen Self-Help Groups and cooperatives, support climate-smart agricultural production and household or cooperative enterprises, facilitate market and service linkages, collect monitoring information, and maintain regular engagement with project participants, government offices, market actors, and other stakeholders. Key Responsibilities:  Community Mobilization, SHGs and Cooperatives Support selection of project areas and participants and facilitate formation, regular functioning, savings, and capacity-building of Self-Help Groups. Facilitate formation and strengthening of cooperatives from SHG members and build the capacity of cooperative management committees in leadership, governance, financial management, business management, conflict management, negotiation, planning, staffing, organizing, and monitoring. Support preparation and implementation of cooperative bylaws, monthly plans, business plans, budgets, savings systems, and fund-utilization arrangements in line with member priorities and government requirements. Promote transparency, participation, accountability, inclusion, and member ownership in day-to-day cooperative operations. Climate-Smart Production and Household Enterprises Facilitate climate-smart production of sesame, onion, garlic, vegetables, tomato, flowers, and other climate-adaptive crops in accordance with project technical guidance. Support demonstration activities, farmer learning, grading, sorting, cleaning, packaging, transportation, and other practices that improve product quality and farmer returns. Facilitate development of viable agro- and non-agro-based enterprises at household and cooperative levels. Support project participants to understand living income, sustainable income, household business planning, and profit analysis. Market Linkage and Private-Sector Engagement Facilitate establishment and operation of collection points and support aggregation and marketing of agricultural products. Develop and maintain working relationships with buyers, sellers, local traders, supermarkets, processors, input companies, exporters, transporters, and other market actors. Facilitate contract-farming and other commercial arrangements between farmers or cooperatives and input, processing, buying, or export companies. Provide or facilitate access to current market information and promote use of relevant mobile applications for learning, production support, and market linkage. Training, Facilitation and Capacity Building Organize and facilitate farmer, SHG, cooperative, and stakeholder training and workshops using approved session guides and materials. Reinforce relevant Heifer Cornerstones and facilitate periodic participatory self-review and planning processes. Support cooperative capacity assessments and ensure practical follow-up on agreed improvement plans. Provide regular coaching, follow-up, and problem-solving support to participants, group leaders, and cooperative committees. Monitoring, Data and Reporting Support baseline, midline, performance evaluation, and other monitoring and learning activities and maintain accurate participant and activity records. Visit SHGs, cooperatives, households, farms, collection points, and enterprises regularly to monitor progress, identify operational or programmatic constraints, and support participatory solutions in consultation with the Project Coordinator and Heifer program team. Prepare accurate monthly, quarterly, annual, activity, training, and field reports and submit them within the required timelines. Maintain appropriate documentation, attendance, participant information, success stories, photos, consent records, and other evidence required by the project. Stakeholder Coordination Build and maintain constructive relationships with Union Parishad, upazila administration, cooperative offices, agriculture and marketing offices, women and children affairs offices, private-sector actors, NGOs, and relevant service providers. Facilitate project meetings, workshops, service-linkage events, and coordination with government and non-government stakeholders. Represent SDS and the project professionally at community and field level and communicate project messages accurately. Expected Key Deliverables Functional SHGs and cooperatives with regular meetings, savings, plans, records, governance practices, and member participation. Timely and quality delivery of farmer training, climate-smart demonstrations, capacity assessments, and agreed follow-up actions. Active collection points, enterprise initiatives, and market or service linkages for project participants and cooperatives. Accurate participant, monitoring, training, field-visit, consent, and project documentation. Timely monthly, quarterly, annual, and activity reports. Respectful, safe, inclusive, and safeguarding-compliant engagement with project participants and communities. Code of Conduct, Safeguarding and Ethical Responsibilities Comply with SDS policies and applicable Heifer requirements on integrity, non-discrimination, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, conflict of interest, confidentiality, data protection, safeguarding, and accurate record-keeping. Maintain professional boundaries, protect the dignity and safety of others, and promptly report concerns through approved channels. SDS and Heifer maintain zero tolerance for sexual exploitation and abuse, harassment, child abuse, abuse of power, and retaliation. Violations may result in disciplinary action, including termination. Employment is subject to satisfactory reference and background checks and compliance with the Code of Conduct. Working Conditions and General Requirements The position is field-based and requires regular travel to remote communities, farms, cooperatives, markets, government offices, and other activity locations in Rajbari District. The position may require flexible working hours during community meetings, training, market activities, data collection, project events, or emergencies. The position holder may be assigned other related duties that are consistent with the purpose and level of the position and the needs of the project. This job description may be reviewed and updated by SDS in consultation with relevant project stakeholders to reflect evolving project or organizational requirements.

Cash Flow & Treasury Management:  Manage working capital, cash flow forecasting, banking facilities, fund allocation, loan management, and liquidity to ensure uninterrupted factory operations. Costing & Profitability Analysis:  Oversee product costing, garment cost analysis, factory overhead allocation, contribution margin, production cost monitoring, and profitability analysis by unit, product, and customer. Accounts & General Ledger:  Ensure accurate and timely maintenance of general ledgers, accounts payable and receivable, bank reconciliation, inventory accounting, fixed assets, depreciation, and month-end and year-end closing. Tax, VAT & Statutory Compliance:  Ensure compliance with applicable Bangladesh tax, VAT, withholding tax, corporate tax, company law, financial reporting requirements, and other relevant statutory obligations within prescribed deadlines. Banking & Trade Finance:  Manage relationships with commercial banks and financial institutions, including working capital facilities, import and export finance, L/C, back-to-back L/C, bank guarantees, export proceeds realization, and foreign currency transactions, as applicable. Export Proceeds & Foreign Exchange:  Monitor export documentation, realization of export proceeds, outstanding bills, foreign currency exposure, and coordination with Commercial and Merchandising teams to support timely financial settlement. Internal Control & Risk Management:  Establish and strengthen financial policies, SOPs, approval matrices, segregation of duties, fraud prevention measures, and internal control systems across all business units. Inventory & Asset Control:  Ensure proper accounting and reconciliation of raw materials, trims, work-in-progress, finished goods, spare parts, fixed assets, and other inventories in coordination with Supply Chain, Commercial, and Factory Operations. Audit Management:  Coordinate internal, external, tax, VAT, and other statutory audits; ensure timely submission of supporting documents and implementation of audit recommendations. Financial Analysis & Business Support:  Provide management with financial insights, investment appraisals, cost-saving opportunities, profitability forecasts, and risk assessments to facilitate strategic business decisions. Payroll & Employee-Related Payments:  Oversee financial controls for payroll, employee benefits, incentives, bonuses, final settlements, and other employee-related payments in coordination with HR and Administration. Accounts Receivable & Payable:  Monitor customer collections, supplier payments, ageing reports, credit exposure, and payment schedules to maintain financial discipline and healthy business relationships. ERP & Process Improvement:  Ensure effective utilization of ERP and accounting systems, strengthen financial data integrity, automate reporting, and improve the efficiency of accounting and financial processes. Team Leadership:  Lead, mentor, and develop the Accounts & Finance team, establish performance targets, delegate responsibilities, and ensure timely and accurate delivery of departmental outputs. Interdepartmental Coordination:  Work closely with Production, Merchandising, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Administration, Procurement, and Factory Management to align financial controls with operational requirements. Management & Board Reporting:  Present financial performance, key financial indicators, cash flow positions, budget variances, business risks, and strategic recommendations to senior management and the Board, as required.

company_business: Peoples Ceramic Industries Ltd. pioneered the manufacturing of porcelain tableware’s in Bangladesh in 1962. The company was established by late Mr Ansar Uddin Ahmed,a Civil Engineer with a view to improving the lives of ordinary people who could not afford to eat off a ceramic plate. European Style tableware’s were chosen for fabrication as they were popular at home & that would create an opportunity to export in due course; PCI tableware’s were welcomed in Holland & United Kingdom in 1981. In the initial years, along with basic house wares items, Tea Cups & Saucers suitable for restaurant use were also fabricated. Marketing the quantity produced posed a big problem & thereafter Late Mr Ahmed opened doors to market them in Pakistan competing against 2 factories there. It was an instant success owing to Hard Grade porcelain products of PCI. Later Institutional products were also added to cater the Hotels and Restaurants. The company always focused on adopting Appropriate Technology and sourcing quality raw materials (from around the world) to keep product cost at a minimum; also machinery and equipments were constantly upgraded to maintain competitive edge. In 2009 company initiated decal printing starting with “Logo” and by 2012 had a full fledged automatic decal printing facility. Peoples Ceramic followed the vision of its founder at every step to provide good quality products to its customers, create a better future for themselves and the nation.

Emerging from the need to address disaster management efforts more efficiently, effectively, and timely, BRAC created a dedicated programme titled "Disaster Environment and Climate Change" in 2008, which was restructured and retitled as Disaster Risk Management Program (DRMP) with an aim to strengthen community resilience through disaster risk reduction and preparedness along with emergency response and recovery actions.
